added_lemmas.statement: Whenever the raw four-snapshot fiber is nonempty, it is finite if and only if \(k_\lambda\leq 1\) for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\); on a finite stratum it contains exactly \(2^q\) candidates before admissibility filtering.  If some \(k_\lambda\geq 2\), every admissible candidate lies in a positive-dimensional relatively open fiber.  On a finite stratum with \(q\geq1\), at most \(2^{q-1}\) raw candidates are admissible, while for \(q=0\) at most one is admissible.  Consequently, in dimension \(p\geq2\), every finite admissible fiber has at most \(2^{p-1}\) members.  This bound is sharp: for every \(p\geq2\), there are strict-decrease Gaussian snapshot laws for which \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}\) has \(2^p\) members and \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\), and hence the compatible structural-explanation fiber, has exactly \(2^{p-1}\) members.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\text{thm:block-certificate}\), a nonempty raw fiber is a product, over \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), of torsors for \(O(k_\lambda)\).  The group \(O(0)\) is a singleton, \(O(1)=\{-1,1\}\), and \(O(k)\) has local dimension \(k(k-1)/2>0\) when \(k\geq2\).  Hence the raw fiber is finite exactly when every \(k_\lambda\leq1\), and then
\[
 \#\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}
 =\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\#O(k_\lambda)
 =2^{\#\{\lambda:k_\lambda=1\}}=2^q.
\]
If some \(k_\lambda\geq2\), the product torsor has positive local dimension at every point.  The three admissibility requirements in \(\text{def:admissible-fiber}\) are strict and relatively open on this torsor.  Indeed, spectral radius is continuous; avoidance of \(( -\infty,0]\) persists when the roots of the characteristic polynomial are perturbed sufficiently little; and, on \(\rho(W)<1\),
\[
 \operatorname{vec}(T_W)
 =\bigl(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\bigr)^{-1}\operatorname{vec}(H_0)
\]
is continuous, so \(C_0-T_W\succ0\) is open.  Thus every admissible candidate on such a stratum lies in a positive-dimensional relatively open fiber.

We next prove the universal finite-fiber upper bound.  Suppose first that \(q\geq1\), and fix a block \(\lambda_0\) with \(k_{\lambda_0}=1\).  In the parameterization of \(\text{thm:block-certificate}\), changing only the sign of the one-dimensional residual isometry in that block defines a fixed-point-free involution of \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}\).  In orthonormal bases adapted to the probe span and its residual complement, this operation multiplies \(\det(O_{\lambda_0})\), and therefore \(\det(W)\), by \(-1\).  The \(2^q\) raw candidates consequently split into \(2^{q-1}\) matrices of each determinant sign.

Every raw candidate is invertible, because \(WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1\) and \(H_0,H_1\succ0\).  If a real invertible matrix \(W\) satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing,
\]
then all of its real eigenvalues are positive, while each nonreal conjugate pair \(z,\overline z\) contributes \(z\overline z=|z|^2>0\) to the determinant.  Hence \(\det(W)>0\).  The logarithm-cut filter therefore rejects every negative-determinant raw candidate, so
\[
 \#\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\leq 2^{q-1}\qquad(q\geq1).
\]
If \(q=0\), the raw fiber itself has one member.  Finally,
\[
 q\leq\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}k_\lambda
 \leq\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}m_\lambda=p.
\]
Together with \(p\geq2\) from \(\text{ass:dimension}\), this gives \(\#\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\leq2^{p-1}\) on every finite stratum, including the case \(q=0\).  By the bijection in \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\), the same bound holds for compatible structural explanations.

It remains to attain the bound while satisfying all strict filters.  Let \(Q_\circ\) be the cyclic permutation matrix defined by
\[
 Q_\circ e_i=e_{i+1}\quad(1\leq i<p),
 \qquad Q_\circ e_p=e_1.
\]
Thus \(Q_\circ\in O(p)\) and \(\det(Q_\circ)=(-1)^{p-1}\).  For a sign matrix
\[
 D=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_p),
 \qquad s_i\in\{-1,1\},
\]
one has
\[
 (Q_\circ D)^p=\left(\prod_{i=1}^p s_i\right)I_p.
\]
If \(\det(Q_\circ D)>0\), then \(\prod_i s_i=(-1)^{p-1}\).  Were \(-1\) an eigenvalue of \(Q_\circ D\), applying the preceding power identity to a corresponding nonzero eigenvector would give
\[
 (-1)^p=\prod_{i=1}^p s_i=(-1)^{p-1},
\]
a contradiction.  Because a real eigenvalue of an orthogonal matrix is either \(-1\) or \(1\), every orientation-preserving \(Q_\circ D\) avoids the negative real axis.

Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  At \(A_0=\alpha I_p\), each matrix \(A_0Q_\circ D\) with \(\det(Q_\circ D)>0\) is stable and avoids \(( -\infty,0]\).  This cut avoidance persists simultaneously for all such \(D\) when a positive diagonal matrix \(A\) is sufficiently close to \(A_0\).  To verify this without a spectral-gap assumption, suppose the contrary for one fixed \(D\).  There would be positive diagonal matrices \(A_n\to A_0\), numbers \(t_n\geq0\), and
\[
 \det(t_nI_p+A_nQ_\circ D)=0.
\]
For all large \(n\), \(\lVert A_n\rVert_2\leq c\) for some \(c<1\).  Since \(-t_n\) is then an eigenvalue of \(A_nQ_\circ D\), \(0\leq t_n\leq c\).  A subsequence has \(t_n\to t\in[0,c]\), and continuity of the determinant would imply
\[
 \det(tI_p+\alpha Q_\circ D)=0,
\]
contradicting the established cut avoidance at \(A_0\).  There are only \(2^{p-1}\) positive-orientation sign matrices, so one neighborhood works for all of them.  Choose within that neighborhood
\[
 A=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_p),
 \qquad 0<\alpha_i<1,
 \qquad \alpha_i^2\neq\alpha_j^2\quad(i\neq j).
\]
For every sign matrix \(D\),
\[
 \lVert AQ_\circ D\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2
 =\max_i\alpha_i<1,
\]
so every raw candidate below is stable; by the choice of \(A\), every positive-determinant one also passes the logarithm-cut filter.

Define zero mean differences and the three covariance differences by
\[
 d_0=d_1=d_2=0,
 \qquad H_0=I_p,
 \qquad H_1=A^2,
 \qquad H_2=AQ_\circ A^2Q_\circ^{\mathsf T}A.
\]
All three \(H_j\) are positive definite, so \(\text{ass:strict-decrease}\) holds.  Moreover
\[
 R=A^2,
 \qquad S=Q_\circ A^2Q_\circ^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The squared diagonal entries of \(A\) are distinct, so the common spectral blocks are one dimensional, with source eigenvectors \(e_i\) and target eigenvectors \(Q_\circ e_i\).  Both probe matrices in every block vanish because all \(d_j\) vanish.  Hence
\[
 m_\lambda=1,\qquad r_\lambda=0,\qquad k_\lambda=1,\qquad q=p.
\]
The block parameterization in \(\text{thm:block-certificate}\) now gives, exactly once each, the \(2^p\) raw matrices
\[
 W_D=AQ_\circ D,
 \qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_p),
 \qquad s_i\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
Directly, their defining equations are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 W_DH_0W_D^{\mathsf T}&=A^2=H_1,\\
 W_DH_1W_D^{\mathsf T}
 &=AQ_\circ DA^2DQ_\circ^{\mathsf T}A
 =AQ_\circ A^2Q_\circ^{\mathsf T}A=H_2,
 \end{aligned}
\]
where \(DA^2D=A^2\); the mean equations hold because the probes are zero.

It remains to realize these differences as positive-definite Gaussian level covariances and to make the reconstructed measurement covariance positive on every branch.  For each of the finitely many sign matrices define
\[
 T_D=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}W_D^j(W_D^{\mathsf T})^j.
\]
The bound \(\lVert W_D\rVert_2<1\) makes this series converge, its zeroth term gives \(T_D\succ0\), and shifting the series proves
\[
 T_D-W_DT_DW_D^{\mathsf T}=I_p=H_0.
\]
Choose a scalar
\[
 c>\max_D\lambda_{\max}(T_D)
\]
and set
\[
 C_0=cI_p,\qquad C_1=C_0-H_0,\qquad
 C_2=C_1-H_1,\qquad C_3=C_2-H_2,\qquad m_0=m_1=m_2=m_3=0.
\]
For each \(D\), put \(E_D=C_0-T_D\).  The choice of \(c\) gives \(E_D\succ0\).  Using the Stein equation and the two raw congruences successively yields, for \(k=0,1,2,3\),
\[
 C_k=W_D^kT_D(W_D^{\mathsf T})^k+E_D\succ0.
\]
Thus the displayed \(C_k\) are well-defined positive-definite observed covariance matrices, their adjacent differences are exactly the prescribed strict positive-definite \(H_j\), and \(E_D\) is a common positive-definite measurement covariance across the four snapshots within each explanation.

Because \(\det(A)>0\), exactly half of the sign matrices satisfy
\[
 \det(W_D)=\det(A)\det(Q_\circ D)>0.
\]
All of these \(2^{p-1}\) candidates pass stability, the logarithm cut, and \(E_D\succ0\), so they belong to \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\).  Every remaining candidate has negative determinant and therefore has a negative real eigenvalue by the conjugate-pair determinant argument above; it fails the logarithm-cut filter.  Hence
\[
 \#\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}=2^{p-1}.
\]
Finally, \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\) reconstructs from every surviving \(W_D\) a unique real Hurwitz generator in the principal-log alias strip, the covariance \(T_D\), the positive common measurement covariance \(E_D\), the equilibrium \(x_D^\star=0\), and the initial mean \(\mu_0=0\).  Its bijection proves that these are exactly \(2^{p-1}\) distinct compatible structural explanations.  This proves attainability and completes the sharp classification.
added_lemmas.justification: The proposition gives the exact worst-case output size, not merely an exponential lower witness, while retaining the finite-versus-continuous stabilizer classification.
added_lemmas.gap: AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 discusses orthogonal blocks but does not derive the residual-rank criterion with two mean probes or the sharp \(2^{p-1}\) maximum after stability, logarithm-cut, Stein, and noise-positivity filtering.
added_lemmas.consumer: A complete snapshot-dynamics solver must be able to return as many as \(2^{p-1}\) scientifically admissible explanations and must report a continuous fiber whenever a residual block has dimension at least two.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The former proposition's attained count \(2^{\lfloor p/2\rfloor}\) is superseded by a replacement that preserves every stabilizer-stratum clause and proves the sharp finite-fiber maximum \(2^{p-1}\); inbound dependencies should therefore migrate to the stronger proved proposition.

prose_updates.tldr: Four independent Gaussian snapshots can identify a stable continuous-time linear mechanism even when every observed covariance contains the same unknown positive-definite measurement component, but the answer is a stratified fiber rather than automatically one matrix. With three snapshots, raw compatibility holds exactly when \(\lVert H_0^{-1/2}d_0\rVert_2=\lVert H_1^{-1/2}d_1\rVert_2\); the compatible transitions form an \(O(p-1)\) torsor when \(d_0\ne0\) and an \(O(p)\) torsor when \(d_0=0\), giving continuous ambiguity generically for \(p\ge3\) and already at \(p=2\) on the zero-displacement elbow. A fourth snapshot identifies generically through the rational map \(K_1K_0^{-1}\), while stability, the principal-logarithm cut, Stein reconstruction, and strict noise positivity decide structural compatibility. The same stabilizer dimension equals information nullity; on finite strata the exact worst-case number of compatible explanations is \(2^{p-1}\), and this bound is attained. Regular branches admit perturbation bounds and Gaussian moment inference. Supplying \(E\) yields this paper's stable, embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise subclass of the broader Aalto--Lamoline--Goncalves model, not equality with that model class. Certified initialization and stable labeling of every noncyclic finite branch remain open.

project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the exact three-snapshot norm certificate and \(O(p-r)\) classification, an if-and-only-if four-snapshot block Gram certificate, a bijective admissibility map, the complete exceptional-stratum classification, and the sharp attainable finite-fiber maximum \(2^{p-1}\), together with rational perturbation theory and branchwise inference. It also identifies the precise supplied-noise subclass relation and retains certified global initialization and branch labeling as the remaining open construction problem.

prose_updates.related_work: AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 provides the closest congruence architecture. Its published class allows known process covariance \(Q\), arbitrary invertible discrete-time dynamics, and finite-second-moment non-Gaussian laws. After a supplied measurement covariance \(E\) is subtracted, the model studied here is only its stable, principal-log-embeddable, Gaussian, \(Q=0\) subclass; the inherited consequence used here is the consecutive latent-covariance congruence, not equality of model classes or an exact reduction to every part of their theorem. It does not provide the present two-probe residual-rank classification or the sharp \(2^{p-1}\) admissible finite-fiber maximum. WangEtAl2024 proves a three-time-point result for deterministic affine dynamics from supplied state moments and motivates the \(\texttt{covar\_lin\_dyn}\) consumer. QWENDY2025 uses four supplied covariance matrices and simple spectra to resolve a homogeneous congruence problem, but it contains neither an unknown common additive covariance nor the exact three-snapshot norm and stabilizer classification proved here. MorimotoKashima2025 and InoueEtAl2026 estimate stochastic linear dynamics from direct snapshot marginals by Schrödinger-bridge optimization without a global common-noise identification certificate. Blevins2017 analyzes continuous-time aliases and motivates the principal-logarithm strip after the transition is recovered. KoltchinskiiLounici2017 supplies spectral perturbation tools, while HauensteinSottile2012 supplies root certificates; neither solves basis-invariant finite-branch enumeration with matrix-inequality filters. ChernozhukovHongTamer2007 and Drton2009 locate set inference and singular asymptotics around the regular-stratum results. KongEtAl2023 studies process and measurement covariance identification from a paired stationary time series with known system matrices, a different information regime from destructive marginal snapshots.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact population conditions--spectral matching, block Gram equality, and the three-snapshot whitened norm equality--must not be imposed as empirical accept-or-reject equalities, because unconstrained noisy sample moments satisfy them with probability zero. On a finite population stratum, the block certificate yields \(2^q\) raw sign completions; when \(q\ge1\), the determinant test removes at least half before the principal-logarithm calculation, and the sharp worst-case admissible output size is \(2^{p-1}\). On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) is the off-model rational estimator used by the perturbation theorem. The radius \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\) guarantees that its full plug-in reconstruction is defined, whereas the smaller radius \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\) also preserves the stability, logarithm, Stein, and reconstructed-covariance positivity filters; neither radius forces noisy moments onto the exact population fiber. On a noncyclic finite stratum, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is a population-branch-centered residual estimator, not a globally implementable branch finder until certified initialization and labeling are solved. The two structural plug-ins are \(\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\) and \(\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}},\widehat z)\), each with initial-mean coordinate \(\widehat m_0\).
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact population three-snapshot norm certificate, its \(O(p-r)\) fibers, the generic four-snapshot frontier, stabilizer dimension, the sharp attainable finite-stratum maximum of \(2^{p-1}\) compatible explanations, the information-nullity identity, cyclic perturbation bounds, and the local regular-branch limit law are theorem-level deliverables. The \(d_0=0\) elbow has continuous \(O(p)\) ambiguity already at \(p=2\); when \(p=2\) and \(d_0\ne0\), the raw fiber is only zero-dimensional and admissibility filters may leave one or more isolated candidates. Any unknown-common-noise supermodel containing the deterministic Gaussian subclass inherits its three-snapshot nonidentification witnesses. Supplying \(E\) gives only the stable, principal-log-embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise subclass of AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022; the broader published class also permits known \(Q\), arbitrary invertible discrete-time transitions, and non-Gaussian finite-second-moment laws. The global certified initializer, complete branch certificate, stable empirical labeling, and simultaneous coverage across all noncyclic finite branches remain open. No uniform inference is claimed at branch collisions, positivity boundaries, logarithm cuts, or stabilizer-dimension jumps, and exact population equalities are not empirical testing rules.

statement_notes.justification: The proposition classifies every exceptional stratum and proves that \(2^{p-1}\) is the exact worst-case number of admissible explanations on a finite stratum.
statement_notes.gap: AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 mentions repeated-eigenvalue orthogonal blocks, but does not give the exact residual-rank criterion after two mean probes or the sharp branch count surviving every dynamical and positivity filter.
statement_notes.consumer: Any complete solver for snapshot dynamics must budget for up to \(2^{p-1}\) scientifically admissible outputs and report continuous fibers rather than silently selecting one model.
